Let \(R\) be the region bounded by the graphs of \(y=\sin (\pi x)\) and \(y=x^{3}-4 x\), as shown in the figure above.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] The horizontal line \(y=-2\) splits the region \(R\) into two parts. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the area of the part of \(R\) that is below this horizontal line.
\item[(c)] The region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For this solid, each cross section perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis is a square. Find the volume of this solid.
\item[(d)] The region \(R\) models the surface of a small pond. At all points in \(R\) at a distance \(x\) from the \(y\)-axis, the depth of the water is given by \(h(x)=3-x\). Find the volume of water in the pond.
\item[(a)] \(\sin (\pi x)=x^{3}-4 x\) at \(x=0\) and \(x=2\)
Area \(=\int_{0}^{2}\left(\sin (\pi x)-\left(x^{3}-4 x\right)\right) d x=4\)
\item[(b)] \(x^{3}-4 x=-2\) at \(r=0.5391889\) and \(s=1.6751309\)
\end{itemize}
The area of the stated region is \(\int_{r}^{s}\left(-2-\left(x^{3}-4 x\right)\right) d x\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c)] Volume \(=\int_{0}^{2}\left(\sin (\pi x)-\left(x^{3}-4 x\right)\right)^{2} d x=9.978\)
\item[(d)] Volume \(=\int_{0}^{2}(3-x)\left(\sin (\pi x)-\left(x^{3}-4 x\right)\right) d x=8.369\) or 8.370
